title: Etale splitting of an integral morphism with finite fibre
statement: Let $\pi:T\to S$ be an integral morphism [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism] of affine schemes [def-pc-scheme] [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Let $s\in S$. Assume that $\pi^{-1}(s)$ is finite and that $\kappa(b)/\kappa(s)$ is finite-dimensional for every $b\in\pi^{-1}(s)$ [def-weil-residue-field] [def-pc-field-extension]. There exist an affine scheme $U$, an etale morphism $g:U\to S$ [def-weil-etale-morphism], a point $u\in U$ with $g(u)=s$, an integer $m\geq0$, and pairwise disjoint open-and-closed affine subschemes $V_1,\ldots,V_m$ whose union is $T\times_SU$ [def-pc-fibre-product], such that each $V_i\to U$ is integral and has exactly one point $v_i$ over $u$, and $\kappa(v_i)/\kappa(u)$ is purely inseparable [def-weil-pbc-finite-purely-inseparable-extension]. The integer $m$ need not equal the number of points of $\pi^{-1}(s)$ before base change; if $m=0$, the union is empty.

proof.text: Enumerate the finite fibre and apply [lem-weil-pbc-etale-split-residue-points]. Flatten its finite family of points to show that the entire new fibre is finite. Its residue extensions are purely inseparable. No injectivity of the flattened family is needed: the next construction enumerates the actual fibre without repetitions.

source.place: Tag 02LM, residue-field splitting, as used in the first proof of Tag 0BSR

proof.text: For an integral affine morphism Spec B → Spec A and a selected fibre prime q, choose for every other fibre prime q′ an element b(q′) in q′ but not in q. Incomparability [lem-weil-pbc-integral-incomparability] supplies these elements. Let C be the A-subalgebra they generate. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-of-integral-generators] it is finite over A. If a fibre prime has the same contraction to C as q, membership of its chosen generator gives a contradiction unless it is q. Thus q is the only point over its image in Spec C within the marked fibre. The construction also works when q is the only fibre point: C is generated by the empty family.

source.place: Tag 0BSR, first proof, finite intermediate algebra separating fibre primes; the singleton variant and the explicit choice of separating elements are written out here

proof.text: The finite morphism Spec C → Spec A has discrete fibres. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-etale-local-finite-at-point-elementary] at the image of q to obtain an elementary étale neighbourhood and a finite open piece with one marked fibre point. Its open inclusion is proper: its composite to the base is finite, and the ambient finite morphism is separated. Therefore the open is closed. Pull it back along Spec B → Spec C. The finite model property from the preceding step and uniqueness of pullback points over a residue-field-preserving base change show that its marked fibre is exactly q. Use [lem-weil-pbc-pointed-etale-neighbourhood-affine-shrink] to make the base affine. For a non-affine original base first restrict to an affine open containing the marked point; integrality makes its inverse image affine. Pullback point uniqueness and residue-field invariance use the private helpers pullback_point_unique and pullback_fst_residue_iso of FinitePiecePersistence, proved from [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-points] and [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-point-residue-field].

source.place: Tag 0BSR, first proof, pulling a finite-model decomposition back to the integral algebra; Tag 02LK, elementary finite neighbourhood of a fibre point

proof.text: Induct on the number of distinct fibre points. For the successor step take the fibre product of the elementary étale neighbourhood for the previous points and the singleton neighbourhood for the last point. A point above the two marked points exists; choose an affine open around it. The composite is elementary étale. Pull back the old clopens and the new singleton clopen, then intersect every old clopen with the complement of the new one. The fibre points are distinct, so this operation preserves their fibre intersections and gives pairwise disjoint clopens. For the empty family choose an affine open neighbourhood on the base and no clopens.

source.place: Tag 0BSR, first proof; elementary finite induction on clopen singleton neighbourhoods supplied explicitly here

proof.text: The closed complement of the union of the clopens has closed image under the integral projection [lem-weil-pbc-integral-spec-closed-map]. The image misses the marked point. Restrict to an affine neighbourhood inside its open complement and pull back the clopens. They now cover, remain disjoint and closed, and retain their singleton fibres. A clopen inclusion is a closed immersion; its composite with an integral morphism is integral, and therefore its domain is affine over the affine base. If the original fibre is empty, the same closed-image removal makes the whole pullback empty.

source.place: Tag 0BSR, first proof, removing the factor with empty fibre; Mathlib IsIntegralHom gives closedness for arbitrary scheme bases

proof.text: Compose the elementary neighbourhood with the residue-splitting neighbourhood and use pullbackLeftPullbackSndIso to transport the affine clopen partition. The projection from the elementary base change and the open inclusions induce residue-field isomorphisms. The commutative residue-field square identifies the old purely inseparable extension with a tower through the new base residue field. IsPurelyInseparable.tower_top gives pure inseparability for its upper extension. All integrality, disjointness and covering assertions transport across the pullback isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 0BSR, first proof, final decomposition and purely inseparable residue extensions; residue-field-square transport written out here

proof_origin.place: Tag 0BSR, first proof: finite intermediate algebra and étale finite-neighbourhood route. Residue splitting is performed first with Tag 02LM; singleton clopens are constructed using Tag 02LK, combined by finite induction, and the empty-fibre remainder is removed by closedness. All steps are proved in Lean, with no new sorry.
